title: Breeding-space contraction accompanies Adélie penguin population decline across two Antarctic systems
core_claim: Adelie population decline in the eligible long-term series is accompanied by non-proportional concentration of breeding effort among fewer effective monitored colony components, replicated from three Palmer islands to a separately frozen Signy endpoint.

torgersen_triangulation.role: physical phenomenon-level triangulation; no census-code to polygon equivalence

novelty_boundary: Do not claim discovery of the Signy population decline or first observation of colony disappearance; those are previously published.
The new contribution is explicit rejection of proportional thinning for the relative breeding distribution and external replication of that endpoint.
Do not claim a first-ever study unless a separate systematic literature audit supports that wording.
mechanism_boundary: No individual movement, public-information use, breeding dispersal or prospecting is identified.
No causal habitat mechanism is identified.
No Allee effect is inferred from small-first disappearance.
Coarse component concentration can coexist with fine-scale fragmentation.
excluded_from_main_paper: Antarctic-wide area x habitat-complex Paper 2 result
beta hierarchy as a headline inference
stop_rule: No new ecological endpoint, concentration index, threshold, lag, tuned window, or rescue analysis may be added to this manuscript. Remaining work is figures, reproducibility, literature positioning, prose revision and journal formatting.
